title: 1 · Sounds, spelling and stress
blurb: Read any Spanish word aloud: the five vowels, the letters that differ from English, and where the stress goes.

title: 2 · Greetings: tú and usted
blurb: Greet anyone at any time of day, introduce yourself, and choose between tú and usted.

title: 3 · Gender and number of nouns
blurb: Tell masculine from feminine nouns, spot the exceptions, and make any noun plural.

title: 4 · el / la, un / una
blurb: Say the, a and some in all their forms, and order food without dropping an article.

title: 5 · Subject pronouns and ser
blurb: Say who you are, where you are from and what you do, with the subject pronouns and ser.

title: 6 · Adjectives: agreement and position
blurb: Describe people and clothes with adjectives that go after the noun and agree with it.

title: 7 · estar: where and how
blurb: Ask where things are and say how you are right now, with estar.

title: 8 · ser vs estar
blurb: Choose between ser and estar, say how you feel, and avoid the words that change meaning.

title: 9 · hay: there is, there are
blurb: Say what there is in a room or a neighborhood with hay, and know when to use está instead.

title: 10 · Present tense: -ar, -er, -ir
blurb: Say what you and other people do, with the right verb ending for each person.

title: 11 · Questions and question words
blurb: Ask yes/no questions and questions with what, where, when, how, who, how many and why.

title: 12 · Numbers, time and prices
blurb: Count to 1,000, tell the time and ask how much something costs.

title: 13 · Possessives and demonstratives
blurb: Say my, your, his, our, this and that, with the form that agrees with the noun.

title: 14 · Irregular present: tener, ir, hacer
blurb: Say your age, that you are hungry or cold, what the weather is like and where you are going.

title: 15 · Stem-changing verbs: quiero, puedo, pido
blurb: Say what you want, prefer and can do, ask a stranger for help, and ask for things.

title: 16 · gustar: me gusta, me gustan
blurb: Say what you and others like, love and dislike, and say what hurts.

title: 17 · Reflexive verbs and daily routine
blurb: Describe your daily routine: when you wake up, get up, shower and go to bed.

title: 18 · a, de, en, con, por, para
blurb: Say where you go, how you travel, whose things they are and who you go with.

title: 19 · muy and mucho: very cold is mucho frío
blurb: Say "very" and "a lot" the Spanish way, including very cold, very hungry and very thirsty.

title: 20 · y, o, pero, porque
blurb: Join your sentences with and, or, but and because, and ask why.

title: 21 · Directions and places in town
blurb: Ask where a place is, and understand right, left, straight ahead, near and far.

title: 22 · ir a + infinitive: plans
blurb: Talk about your plans: what you are going to do tomorrow, on Saturday or next week.

title: 23 · Object pronouns: lo, la, los, las
blurb: Say "it", "them", "him" and "her" without repeating the noun: Lo compro, La voy a comprar.

title: 24 · The preterite: what you did
blurb: Say what you did yesterday, last night or last weekend, with regular verbs and fui, hice, tuve.

title: 25 · Impersonal se: se habla español
blurb: Read signs and ask general questions: Se habla español, Se venden casas, ¿Cómo se dice…?

title: 26 · Hearing Caribbean Spanish
blurb: Recognize words you already know in fast Dominican and Caribbean speech, plus four everyday local words.
